newsitem.title: USA: U.S. renews reward over Greek killings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. renews reward over Greek killings.

text.p: The United States Wednesday renewed its appeal for Greek citizens to cooperate in providing information about terrorist acts in their country for which Washington is offering $2 million in reward money.

Although the United States first offered the $2 million some time ago, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said it was being renewed in order to help Athens solve the murder of Greek shipowner Costi Peraticos who was buried on May 31.

He was reported to be the 21st person shot by a group calling itself November 17, the same group that claimed credit for killing four Americans -- Richard Welch, George Tsantes, William Nordeen and Ronald Stewart -- over the last 22 years.
In addition, there have been injuries to 28 other Americans, and a rocket attack on the U.S. embassy in Athens in February 1996 was attributed to November 17.

"The government of the United States as part of its efforts to work in close cooperation with the government in Greece, is renewing its appeals to the Greek people for information regarding terrorists acts against American citizens and American property under our counter terrorism rewards programme," Burns said.

"Now we are...reissuing this $2 million reward because just two weeks ago, unfortunately, there was another assassination in Athens of a Greek shipbuilder, Mr. Peraticos, and we very much want to help the Greek government locate the people who are responsible for his murder," he said.
Burns said the November 17 group had claimed responsibility for the murder, as they had with the murders of the four Americans.
"And we mean business," he said. "We mean to help the Greek government, work very closely with the Greek government to locate these people."
Anyone with information about the crimes was asked to contact the U.S. government. Officials said confidentiality was guaranteed.
